headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from Roo Code into unstructured; shared filesystem and broad tool access make default pair unsafe for unverified handoffs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write the VS Code workspace and use MCP, while unstructured reads documents and can write files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Roo Code ingests unstructured outputs from shared files. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Roo Code reads unstructured output files as instructions
IF both agents share the same workspace directory
mitigations: Separate input and output directories per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on unstructured output
Use file naming conventions that distinguish data from instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, and has broad network egress; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If they share a workspace, sensitive content can flow from Roo Code into unstructured outputs or vice versa. The profiles do not show hard isolation between them.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem workspace
IF source code or screenshots are placed into unstructured input documents
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Run unstructured only on sanitized copies
Store screenshots in a separate restricted folder
Rotate API keys if they were ever written to disk
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Roo Code also modifies git state and runs shell commands, while unstructured writes files in a docker container. If they target the same directory or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. No locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or output directory
IF Roo Code performs git operations while unstructured writes artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Pause one agent during git commits
Use a lock file around shared writes
Review diffs before committing
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; unstructured can transform documents and images. If unstructured consumes Roo Code output without verification, errors or hallucinations can propagate into downstream documents or code changes. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF unstructured treats Roo Code output as authoritative input
IF Roo Code writes facts into files that unstructured later republishes
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use
Compare outputs against original sources
Mark generated files as untrusted
Limit unstructured to extraction-only mode
requires-engineering: add validation checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while unstructured processes documents, images, and text. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern exists if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated documents or screenshots are processed through the shared workflow
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pair
Document retention for shared outputs
Delete temporary artifacts after processing
Confirm vendor privacy terms before use
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved processors
